identity.title: Span-Based Optimal Sample Complexity for Weakly Communicating and General Average Reward MDPs

problem.claim: Determine the sample complexity of learning an ε-optimal policy in average-reward MDPs under a generative model.

gap.claim: Existing weakly communicating MDP results either assume uniformly bounded mixing times for all policies or have suboptimal parameter dependence.

contributions.claim: Establishes a weakly communicating MDP bound of Õ(SA H/ε²), claimed minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors in S, A, H, and ε.
Initiates general multichain average-reward analysis by introducing transient-time parameter B, with an Õ(SA(B+H)/ε²) upper bound and matching up-to-logs minimax lower bound.
Reduces average-reward problems to discounted MDPs and derives discounted bounds with quadratic rather than cubic horizon dependence for a fixed instance.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their weakly communicating result is the first minimax-optimal result up to logarithmic factors in all listed parameters, and that the general setting requires a new transient-time parameter and new reduction ideas.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an Õ(SA H/ε²) complexity bound for weakly communicating MDPs.
The authors report an Õ(SA(B+H)/ε²) bound and a matching up-to-logarithmic-factors minimax lower bound for general MDPs.

For discounted MDPs, the authors report bounds Õ(SA H/((1−γ)²ε²)) for weakly communicating instances and Õ(SA(B+H)/((1−γ)²ε²)) for general instances, yielding quadratic horizon dependence for a fixed MDP instance rather than contradicting the general cubic minimax lower bound.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies learning ε-optimal policies in average-reward MDPs with a generative model.
It gives an Õ(SA H/ε²) bound and presents it as minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors across S, A, H, and ε.
It extends the discussion to multichain MDPs, argues that transient time B is necessary, and reports matching upper and lower bounds.
Both results use an average-to-discounted reduction, supported by improved discounted-MDP bounds with quadratic horizon dependence.

source_observation.claim: The abstract ties each complexity bound to explicit structural parameters: bias span H, and in the general setting transient time B in addition to H.

lessons.interpretation: Making the parameters governing difficulty explicit can clarify both scope and why a stronger guarantee is needed.
lessons.application: When presenting a learning-theoretic result, define the instance-dependent quantities in the bound and explain which additional parameter appears when assumptions are relaxed.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the relevant structural parameters are unavailable, unobservable, or not central to the intended use.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the precise definitions of H and B, the generative-model assumptions, or the logarithmic factors.
The discounted lower-bound comparison and the sense in which the bounds circumvent it are not detailed beyond the stated fixed-instance quadratic scaling.

editorial_revisions.before: For discounted MDPs, the authors report sufficient sample bounds scaling with (1−γ)⁻² and state that these circumvent the known (1−γ)⁻³ minimax lower bound.
editorial_revisions.after: For discounted MDPs, the authors report bounds Õ(SA H/((1−γ)²ε²)) for weakly communicating instances and Õ(SA(B+H)/((1−γ)²ε²)) for general instances, yielding quadratic horizon dependence for a fixed MDP instance rather than contradicting the general cubic minimax lower bound.
